verdicts.decision_note: The client explicitly defines the enclosure's contents, mounting, display opening, airflow, and LED-light transmission.
The client explicitly leaves the display size, and therefore the cutout size, unresolved between 1.5 and 2.9 inches.
The client adds independent enclosure constraints for easy assembly and drop-resistant component retention; no existing keys become obsolete.
The client explicitly makes the enclosure conform to the finalized board orientation and connector layout.
The client explicitly states that the battery sits alongside the PCB, establishing an enclosure arrangement constraint without invalidating an existing key.
The client replaces the prior three-board configuration with one integrated board plus sensors, buttons, and LEDs; updating the existing list-valued keys prevents stale three-board semantics.
The client identifies a concrete enclosure-access constraint: the case must not block insertion of the battery cable beside the USB opening.
